bindings.label: A two-year-old boy was referred due to a distal diaphyseal fracture of the left femur

The patient is a two-year-old boy, the first child of non-consanguineous parents; his mother was a 26-year-old primigravida with no history of spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, or neonatal mortalities, married to a 27-year-old unrelated man

At birth, his weight, length, and occipital-frontal circumference were around the 25th percentile; he had plagiocephaly treated with a cranial band (Care band) worn 23 hours per day until age one, with no skull radiographs taken at that time
He had motor delay but other developmental skills were within normal range; there was no history of visual, auditory, or other neurological symptoms, anorexia, weight loss, or muscular hypotonia

Examination at age two showed frontal bossing and slight facial asymmetry with incomplete auricular folding; there were no signs of leontiasis ossea, Cushingoid facies, macrocephaly, retarded growth, or muscular hypotonia

Neurological, ophthalmological, and auditory evaluations were normal; no seizures or non-motor developmental delay; audiometric evaluation ruled out peripheral hearing loss; ophthalmological examination showed normal vision with no strabismus; musculoskeletal examination revealed relative ligamentous hyperlaxity with patellar instability and thoraco-lumbar scoliosis of 32 degrees
